label: Has tag
summary: Whether a decision group type carries the tag given as the argument.
details: Vanilla's decisions window checks it for the tags 'extra_big_button' and 'big_button' to size a decision group's rows and buttons: the largest size for the first tag, a middle one for the second, and a default size when neither is set (row heights 70, 60 and 50).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tag to look for, written as a quoted text.
fields.values: a quoted tag name such as 'big_button'

label: Decision group itself
summary: The decision group type object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Decision with parameters itself
summary: A reference to the decision-with-parameters object itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Command description
summary: A text, the command description of this decision for the player.
details: The decisions window shows this text in a label, and the label is hidden when the text is empty.

label: Decision type
summary: The decision (its type) that this entry with parameters belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the decisions window, and in the faith window to ask whether the decision is shown for the player. Going by its name and these uses, it leads from the parameterised decision to the plain decision.

label: Is possible for player
summary: Whether the decision is possible for the player right now.
details: The decisions window uses it to show one version of an entry when it is possible and another one (through Not) when it is not.

label: Decision with parameters itself
summary: The decision-with-parameters object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla passes it to OpenGameViewData together with 'decision_detail', which opens the decision detail view for that decision (faith window and holy site window).

label: Decision widget itself
summary: A reference to the decision view widget itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Decision widget itself
summary: The decision view widget object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Option list itself
summary: A reference to the option-list widget of a decision itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Option entries
summary: The list of options a decision's option-list widget offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of a list in decision widgets such as the artifact commission and the conversion to mandala, so the interface draws one row per entry.

label: Select option
summary: Selects the given entry in the decision's option list.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it on click with the entry of the clicked row (Entry.Self).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an option entry, in vanilla Entry.Self

label: Option list itself
summary: The option-list widget object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Barony selector itself
summary: A reference to the barony-selection widget of a decision itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Current barony
summary: The barony title currently chosen in the barony-selection widget.
details: Vanilla shows its name without the tier word (GetNameNoTier) in the create holy order decision.

label: Has chosen barony
summary: Whether a barony is currently chosen in the barony-selection widget.
details: The create holy order decision uses it, together with IsCreate or IsRevoke, to decide which parts of the widget to show.

label: Has valid baronies
summary: Whether there is something the barony-selection widget can offer to choose.
details: Vanilla enables the 'change capital' button of the create holy order decision with it. A tooltip uses it to pick between the texts 'Select Holding' (when true) and 'No available Holdings' (when false). Going by its name, it is true when at least one barony can be chosen.

label: Is create mode
summary: Whether the barony-selection widget is in its creating mode.
details: Going by its name and its use in the create holy order decision, the widget has a create mode and a revoke mode (IsRevoke). Vanilla shows parts of the widget only in create mode and only when a barony is chosen.

label: Is revoke mode
summary: Whether the barony-selection widget is in its revoking mode.
details: Going by its name and its use in the create holy order decision, it is the counterpart of IsCreate. Vanilla shows parts of the widget only in revoke mode and only when a barony is chosen.

label: Select capital
summary: Runs the widget's action for selecting the capital barony.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the 'change capital' button of the create holy order decision. Going by its name, it starts the choice of the capital barony.

label: Barony selector itself
summary: The barony-selection widget object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Object selector itself
summary: A reference to the object-selection widget of a decision itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Selectable entries
summary: The list of objects (artifacts, characters, holy sites and so on) a decision lets the player choose from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of the list in the select artifact, select character and select holy site decision widgets, so the interface draws one row per entry.

label: Select object
summary: Selects the given entry as the decision's chosen object.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it on click with the clicked row (SelectScopeObjectEntry.Self).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a selection entry, in vanilla SelectScopeObjectEntry.Self

label: Object selector itself
summary: The object-selection widget itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Title selector itself
summary: A reference to the title-selection widget of a decision itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Current title
summary: The title currently chosen in the title-selection widget.
details: Going by its name and the lines where the same function is used on the related barony and title-of-tier widgets (shown as a title name without its tier word), it leads to the chosen title. The input shows no use on this exact type.

label: Has chosen title
summary: Whether a title is currently chosen in the title-selection widget.
details: Going by its name and the same function on the related title-of-tier widget (which picks the text 'change' or 'select' and shows parts of the widget), it answers whether a choice exists. The input shows no use on this exact type.

label: Has valid titles
summary: Whether there is at least one title that can be chosen in the title-selection widget.
details: Going by its name and the same function on related widgets (used to enable a select button), it tells if anything can be picked. The input shows no use on this exact type.

label: Title selector itself
summary: The title-selection widget object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Tier title selector itself
summary: A reference to the widget that selects a title of a given tier, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Current title
summary: The title currently chosen in the title-of-tier selection widget.
details: Vanilla shows its name without the tier word (GetNameNoTier) in the generic title selector widget of decisions.

label: Has chosen title
summary: Whether a title is currently chosen in the title-of-tier selection widget.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the widget only when a title is chosen, and to pick the button text 'Change Title' (a title is chosen) or 'Select Title' (none yet).

label: Has valid titles
summary: Whether there is at least one title that can be chosen in the widget.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the select title button of the generic title selector widget.

label: Select title
summary: Runs the widget's action for selecting a title.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the select title button of the generic title selector widget. Going by its name, it starts the choice of a title.

label: Tier title selector itself
summary: The title-of-tier selection widget object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Decisions view itself
summary: A reference to the decisions view itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close
summary: Closes the decisions window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the close button of the decisions window.

label: Available great projects
summary: The list of available great projects, shown in the decisions window.
details: Vanilla checks with IsDataModelEmpty whether this list, the planned list and the ongoing list are all empty, to show or hide the great projects part of the window.

label: Character
summary: The character whose decisions the window shows.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other windows (used there to reach the character and then its name), it leads from the view to a character. The input shows no use on this exact type.

label: Decision groups
summary: The list of decision groups the decisions window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of the container that holds the decision groups (each drawn as a foldout), so the interface draws one entry per group.

label: Ongoing great projects
summary: The list of great projects that are currently under way, shown in the decisions window.
details: Going by its name, it is the 'ongoing' list next to the available and planned ones. Vanilla checks whether all three lists are empty to show or hide the great projects part of the window.

label: Planned great projects
summary: The list of great projects that are planned, shown in the decisions window.
details: Vanilla checks with IsDataModelEmpty whether this list, the available list and the ongoing list are all empty, to show or hide the great projects part of the window.

label: Is great projects tab active
summary: Whether the great projects tab of the decisions window is the one shown.
details: Going by its name and its pair SetGreatProjectsTabActive. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Selected tab
summary: A text naming the tab currently selected in the decisions window.
details: Vanilla passes it as the variable name to GetVariableSystem.Set (value 'true') when the window starts, so the selected tab is also kept as a variable of the interface.

label: Decisions view itself
summary: The decisions view object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Set great projects tab
summary: Switches the decisions window to the great projects tab (yes) or away from it (no).
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it when the great projects tab content is shown (with (bool)yes) and when it is hidden (with (bool)no), so the view always knows whether that tab is the active one.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the great projects tab should be active.

label: Decision row itself
summary: A reference to one row of the decisions window itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Character
summary: The character this row of the decisions window belongs to.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other windows (used there to reach the character and then its name), it leads to a character. The input shows no use on this exact type.

label: Decision
summary: The decision this row of the decisions window stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a decision row, so the row's parts read the decision's data.

label: Decision picture
summary: The picture shown for this decision row.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of picture elements in the decisions window.

label: Is possible for player
summary: Whether the decision of this row is possible for the player right now.
details: The decisions window uses it to show one version of the row when possible and another one (through Not) when not.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this row of the decisions window is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed (down) state of the row's button.

label: Select row
summary: Selects this row in the decisions window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it when the row is clicked.

label: Decision row itself
summary: The decisions window row object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: War window itself
summary: A reference to the declare war window itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can afford costs
summary: Whether the player can pay the costs of declaring this war.
details: Vanilla shows a warning when it is false (through Not), and also takes it into account for the warnings shown once a casus belli (the reason for the war) is picked.

label: Can send
summary: Whether the war declaration can be sent now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the send button of the declare war window and to switch on an animation on that button.

label: Can show war goal part
summary: Whether the part of the window that shows the war goal can be displayed.
details: Vanilla shows that part when this is true, and for one part also only when a casus belli is selected.

label: Close
summary: Closes the declare war window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the close button.

label: Defender's top liege might join
summary: Whether the defender's top liege (highest overlord) might join the war later.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of an info box marked in the file as the 'liege might join' info.

label: Ally list
summary: The ally list part of the declare war window, as an AllyListSubview.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the allies area in the declare war window.

label: Attacker
summary: The character who declares the war.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the attacker's parts of the declare war window.

label: Casus belli items
summary: The list of casus belli (war reasons) the player can pick from in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of the casus belli list, so the interface draws one row per item.

label: Casus belli type
summary: The casus belli type currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla reads further values from it: whether a white peace is possible, and whether the attacker's or the defender's faith might join the war.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The confirmation window of the character interaction behind this declare war window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the parts that show the interaction's shared confirmation data. Going by its name, the declare war window is built on that window type.

label: Claimant
summary: A character, the claimant, shown in a part of the declare war window.
details: Vanilla uses it only as the data context of one part of the window. Going by its name, it is the claimant of the claim the war is about; the input says nothing more.

label: Confirm click sound
summary: The sound played when the declare war button is clicked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the click sound of the send button.

label: Cost breakdown
summary: The detailed breakdown of one kind of cost (such as piety) of declaring the war.
details: Vanilla passes 'piety' and uses the result as a data context for the piety cost tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted cost name, in vanilla 'piety'

label: Cost description
summary: A text describing the cost of declaring the war.
details: Going by its name, it is the text of the costs. The input shows no use on this exact type; other windows use the same name for their own cost texts.

label: Effects text
summary: The text that describes the effects shown on the currently selected effects tab.
details: The window has victory, defeat and white peace effect tabs. Vanilla shows this text in the effects area.

label: Effects heading
summary: The heading text of the currently selected effects tab.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label above the effects of the tab.

label: Main outcome text
summary: The text that describes the main outcome of the currently selected effects tab.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the effects area of the window.

label: Declare button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the declare war button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the send button.

label: Defender
summary: The character the war is declared on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the defender's parts of the declare war window.

label: Defender and top liege text
summary: A text describing how the defender relates to their top liege (highest overlord).
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window. Going by its name, the text is about the relation between the defender and the top liege.

label: Defender's top liege
summary: The top liege (highest overlord) of the defender.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, once through GetCharacter to reach the character itself.

label: Defenders
summary: The list of defenders in the war.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of a list in the window and hides the list when it is empty.

label: Window header
summary: The header text of the declare war window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text at the top of the window.

label: Military strength text
summary: A text giving the military strength shown in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window. Going by its name, it is the text version of the data that GetMilitaryStrengthInfo offers.

label: Military strength info
summary: The military strength comparison of the war's sides, as a GuiMilitaryStrength object.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the military strength part of the window.

label: Overlord join acceptance
summary: A number for how willing an overlord is to join the war.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Pick prompt
summary: A text asking the player to pick something in the window.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Protect vassal interaction
summary: The interaction used to protect a vassal in the declare war window.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Protect vassal breakdown
summary: A text breaking down why a liege would or would not join the war to protect a vassal.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip. Going by the related value function used in the war messages, the breakdown belongs to that number.

label: Protect vassal value
summary: A number for how strongly the liege would join the war to protect the vassal.
details: Vanilla shows it in the messages 'will join the war' and 'will not join the war', and shows a part of the window when it is greater than 0. Going by those uses, a value above 0 means the liege joins.

label: Selected casus belli
summary: The casus belli item currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads its label, for example to compare it with the name of a specific casus belli.

label: Specific cost
summary: The amount of one kind of cost (such as piety) of declaring the war.
details: Vanilla passes 'piety', hides the piety cost when it is 0, and shows the number without decimals.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted cost name, in vanilla 'piety'

label: Title items
summary: The list of title items shown in the window for choosing the war goal.
details: Vanilla uses it as the datamodel of a grid in the part with the 'choose war goal' instruction, so the interface draws one entry per item.

label: Warning tooltip text
summary: A text for the warning tooltip of the window.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use on this type; the same name on an interaction item is used as a tooltip.

label: Has cost
summary: Whether declaring this war costs anything.
details: Vanilla shows cost parts when it is true and other parts when it is false (through Not).

label: Has no valid casus belli
summary: Whether the window has no valid casus belli (war reason) to offer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of a 'no valid casus bellis' text, shown in the part where a casus belli is chosen.

label: Has selected casus belli
summary: Whether a casus belli (war reason) has been selected in the window.
details: Vanilla shows some parts only when it is true and others when it is not (through Not).

label: Has title items
summary: Whether the war has titles it can be fought for.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use on this type; the same name on a character list item is used as a visibility check.

label: Is breaking alliance
summary: Whether declaring this war would break an alliance.
details: Vanilla uses it in the condition that decides whether to show a warning once a casus belli is selected, together with the cost and truce checks.

label: Is breaking truce
summary: Whether declaring this war would break a truce.
details: Vanilla uses it in the condition that decides whether to show a warning once a casus belli is selected, together with the cost and alliance checks.

label: Is defeat tab
summary: Whether the defeat tab of the war effects is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the defeat tab button.

label: Is victory tab
summary: Whether the victory tab of the war effects is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the victory tab button.

label: Is white peace tab
summary: Whether the white peace tab of the war effects is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the white peace tab button.

label: Are war effects expanded
summary: Whether the war effects part of the window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it to choose the frame of the expand arrow (BoolTo1And2) and to show or hide parts of the window.

label: War window itself
summary: The declare war window object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Send declaration
summary: Sends the war declaration.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the declare war button.

label: Show defeat tab
summary: Switches the war effects to the defeat tab.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the defeat tab button.

label: Show victory tab
summary: Switches the war effects to the victory tab.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the victory tab button.

label: Show white peace tab
summary: Switches the war effects to the white peace tab.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the white peace tab button.

label: Show extra warning
summary: Whether an additional warning should be shown in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the warning area; the text itself comes from WriteAdditionalWarningMessage.

label: Show allies of character
summary: Shows the allies of the given character in the window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it on click with the clicked character item.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose allies to show.
fields.values: a character item, in vanilla CharacterItem.Self

label: Toggle hook
summary: Switches the hook checkbox of the window on or off.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the checkbox click. Going by its name, the hook is the one the player can spend when declaring the war.

label: Toggle war effects
summary: Expands or collapses the war effects part of the window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it on click; IsWarEffectsExpanded tells the current state.

label: Titles are exclusive
summary: Whether the titles of the war exclude each other, so only one can be chosen.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Extra warning text
summary: The text of the additional warning shown in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it in the warning area, which ShouldShowAdditionalWarning switches on.

label: Deferred decision itself
summary: A reference to the deferred decision object itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Decision
summary: The decision that a deferred decision stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a tooltip (cooltip), so the tooltip reads that decision's data.

label: Deferred decision itself
summary: The deferred decision object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Heir window itself
summary: A reference to the designate heir window itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can designate
summary: Whether the chosen heir can be designated now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the designate button of the window.

label: Close
summary: Closes the designate heir window.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the close button in the window's header and from the close button at its bottom.

label: Designate heir
summary: Designates the chosen character as heir.
details: It is an action, not a value. Vanilla calls it from the designate button of the window.

label: Cost description
summary: A text describing the cost of designating an heir.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window.

label: Designate tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the designate button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the designate button.

label: Heirs
summary: The heirs the designate heir window works with.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the whole window content. Going by its name, it leads to the heirs or heir candidates.

label: Heir window itself
summary: The designate heir window object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Designer coat of arms itself
summary: A reference to the designer's coat of arms object itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms that the ruler designer holds, as a CoatOfArms object.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the ruler designer window, and also asks it for its picture (GetTexture, here 124 by 124).

label: Is set
summary: Whether the ruler designer already has a coat of arms.
details: Vanilla shows the coat of arms part when it is true and another part (through Not) when it is not.

label: Designer coat of arms itself
summary: The designer's coat of arms object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Destiny character itself
summary: A reference to the destiny character object itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Character
summary: The character this destiny entry (a possible choice in the succession event window) stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, checks its IsValid to enable the entry and to choose its look (clickable or weak).

label: Type key
summary: The key (internal name) of the destiny type, as a text.
details: Going by its name only. The input shows no use of it in the game's files.

label: Type name
summary: The display name of the destiny type, as a text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the succession event window and compares it with the name of the currently selected destiny character, to decide between a select and an unselect text.

label: Type tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the destiny type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the succession event window.

label: Destiny character itself
summary: The destiny character object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Vanilla passes it to SuccessionEventWindow.SelectDestinyCharacter on click, which makes that entry the selected one.

label: Detail data itself
summary: A reference to the detail data object itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more. It is in the engine's internal GUI category.

label: Error count
summary: The number of errors of the map's detail data (the terrain material textures), as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Errors: ..." in the detail data panel of the engine's map editor.

label: Is updating
summary: Whether the map editor is rebuilding the detail data textures right now.
details: While it is true, vanilla disables the panel's settings, hides the Repack button and shows a waiting spinner instead.

label: Material intensity bias
summary: The intensity bias of the detail data, a decimal number.
details: In the map editor's detail data panel it is shown in the "Intensity bias" box, whose tooltip says it controls how strongly high-intensity materials are preferred when the detail textures are built.

label: Materials limit
summary: The current limit of terrain materials per detail pixel, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with each offered limit to tick the chosen one in the map editor's "Material limit" choices.

label: Repack
summary: Rebuilds (repacks) the detail data textures of the map.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Repack button of the map editor's detail data panel; the button is disabled while an update runs. It returns nothing.

label: Detail data itself
summary: The detail data object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Set material intensity bias
summary: Sets the material intensity bias of the detail data to the given number.
details: Going by its name only. It is an action in the engine's internal GUI category and the game's files do not use it.

label: Set intensity bias
summary: Sets the material intensity bias from the text typed into its box.
details: Vanilla runs it when the user finishes editing the "Intensity bias" box of the map editor's detail data panel; the box passes its text itself, so no argument is written. It returns nothing.

label: Set materials limit
summary: Sets the limit of terrain materials per detail pixel to the given number.
details: Vanilla runs it when the user clicks one of the offered limits, passing that limit's number.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: The new limit of materials per detail pixel.
fields.values: a whole number; vanilla passes one of the supported limits

label: Supported materials limits
summary: The list of limits of materials per detail pixel that can be chosen.
details: Vanilla builds one choice per entry in the map editor's "Material limit" row, each showing the number. The game lists no return type.

label: Barter icon itself
summary: A reference to the detailed barter map icon itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.

label: Barter mission
summary: The barter mission that the map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the map icon, and reads its estimated completion time (GetEta) in the ongoing barter mission tooltip.

label: Loot
summary: The amount of loot the barter mission would bring.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number without decimals in the barter icon tooltips (the potential mission and the province tooltip).

label: Province
summary: The province the barter icon is on.
details: Vanilla reads from it the province's name, the barter goods needed and the loot received, in the icon's tooltips and map pins.

label: Has barter mission
summary: Whether the icon has a barter mission.
details: Vanilla uses it, together with the map zoom level, to decide when the detailed icon is shown.

label: Barter icon itself
summary: The detailed barter icon object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name, it hands the object on to another function. The game documents nothing more and the input shows no use on this type.

label: Confirmation view itself
summary: A reference to the detailed confirmation view itself, for use in the interface.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents nothing more.
